rationale: Crum 99a 'field.' In landscape-inventory triplet with 'mountains' and 'waters,' giving the natural-cosmographic loci from which the living soul is drawn upward.
Greek loanword φοσσᾶτον (Latin fossatum). Cosmographic term for the great upper assembly compared to a fortified military camp. Stands in parallel/contrast to other cosmic gathering-terms.

Possessable noun with possessive prefix ⲡⲉⲩ-. Context (something taken upward, related to upward conveyance) suggests an extracted substance/draught. Etymology unclear — possibly related to a substance-noun or specialized cosmographic term. Confidence low.

Verbal root for the eschatological extraction of light-substance from matter. Used here in tandem with ⲥⲩⲗⲁ 'plunder' (Greek συλάω). Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲱⲗⲕ̄/ⲱⲗϫ 'snatch, draw out.' Preserves the upward-removal semantics of the redemptive reaping.

ⲥⲁⲣⲏⲥ = ⲥⲁ-ⲣⲏⲥ 'side-of-south.' Specific cosmographic designation in this kephalaion: 'this world of the south' is the unique region in which the trees and the small thing of the upper place exist. Cardinal-direction term parallel to ⲡⲥⲁⲛ̄ⲧⲡⲉ 'upper place,' ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'lower place.'
Reduplicated form of ϣⲱⲡ 'swallow, consume.' Used of Matter consuming her own members at the eschatological dissolution. The reduplication intensifies the swallowing/devouring.
Reduplicated of ⲥⲱⲕ 'draw, pull.' Continuous-iterative aspect: 'drawing each other's life through the energy of the powers.' Standard Coptic intensification pattern.
